topic: Right-triangle trigonometry: tangent from two given sides
problem: In right triangle RST, angle T is the right angle, RT = 20, and RS = 29. What is the value of tan(S)?

bad.why: No angle measure is given, so there is nothing to type into tan( ) directly; the angle would first have to be found with inverse trig.

algebraFirst.description: Computes the missing leg by hand, sqrt(841 - 400) = sqrt(441) = 21, then writes tan(S) = opposite/adjacent = 20/21.

explanationNotes: Name the sides from angle S's point of view: RT is across from S (opposite), ST touches S and is not the hypotenuse (adjacent), and RS is across from the right angle (hypotenuse). Desmos finds the missing leg ST = 21 with the Pythagorean theorem from the reference sheet, so tan(S) = opposite/adjacent = 20/21; 21/20 would be the tangent of the other acute angle, R.
